does: Cuts shallow lines through skin or fat, so that the fat can melt out and the skin crisps without curling.

intro.what: Scoring makes shallow cuts through skin or fat without cutting into the flesh.
intro.why: It teaches you to control knife depth so fat can render and skin can crisp without unnecessary damage below.

how: Chill the piece so that the fat is firm.
Draw a sharp knife across the fat in parallel lines a finger apart, cutting through the fat but not into the flesh.
Turn the piece and cut across the first lines to make diamonds.

cues.text: A neat pattern of diamonds, with white fat in every cut and no red flesh showing.

mistakes.mistake: Cutting into the flesh, so that the meat loses juice and dries where it was cut.
mistakes.fix: Use the tip of the knife with a light hand, and stop when the colour changes.

quiz.question: What is scoring skin or fat intended to encourage?
choices: Deep cuts through the flesh for portioning.
Keeping melted fat trapped under the skin.
quiz.because: Shallow openings allow fat to escape and reduce the pull that can curl skin.

quiz.question: Why chill the piece before scoring?
choices: Soft warm fat guides the knife more evenly.
Chilling makes deep flesh cuts necessary.
Firm fat is easier to cut precisely.
quiz.because: Firm fat offers a more controlled surface for shallow knife work.

quiz.question: Which appearance suggests cuts stayed within the fat?
choices: White fat in the cuts without red flesh showing.
Red flesh visible along every line.
Deep gaps passing through the piece.
quiz.because: The colour beneath each cut helps distinguish fat from flesh.

quiz.question: The knife keeps cutting into the meat. What should change?
choices: Press harder to keep all cuts equally deep.
Use a light hand and stop when the colour changes.
Warm the fat until it smears.
quiz.because: Light shallow cuts preserve the flesh while opening the fat layer.
